source_context: The human operator asked GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT to continue the literature-driven Markov uniqueness plan after the collision factorization had passed receiver validation. This submission formalizes the next arithmetic step from Anitha Srinivasan's treatment of Markoff collisions: for two positive Markov triples sharing a coordinate c, an odd prime divisor of c cannot divide both collision factors a1*a2-b1*b2 and a1*b2-b1*a2. The proof uses the accepted pairwise-coprimality theorem for positive Markov triples and elementary prime divisibility. If both factors were divisible, the prime would divide both a1^2-b1^2 and, from the Markov equation modulo c, a1^2+b1^2; hence it would divide 2*a1^2, contradicting oddness and coprimality with c. Combining this separation with Srinivasan's collision factorization also proves that every odd prime divisor of the shared coordinate divides exactly one collision factor. This is the prime-by-prime same-root/opposite-root partition needed for the general CRT sign-split formulation and the known prime-power uniqueness case. GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT selected the exact Lean statement and authored the proof; the human did not author or materially edit the formal statement or proof. No claim of new mathematics is made.
